findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will raise TypeError on instantiation
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Since none are implemented, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` remains abstract and `Detector.detector_handler` (which does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` whenever a metric alert detector is processed. Previously the handler returned an empty list and was harmless. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or don't register the handler yet.

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise ValueError for unmapped DetectorPriorityLevel values
findings.body: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` converts a `DetectorPriorityLevel` into a `PriorityLevel` purely by numeric value. If the two enums ever diverge (e.g. a DetectorPriorityLevel value with no corresponding PriorityLevel member), this raises ValueError inside detector evaluation and aborts processing of the data packet. An explicit mapping (or a validated helper) would make the coupling safe and explicit.

findings.title: Multi-group test builds expected occurrence with the wrong value
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, group_2's data value is 10 but the expected occurrence is built with `value=6`. The assertion only passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`, so the test would not catch a handler that mixes up group values. Pass the real value (10) so the expectation is meaningful.
